extract complex features from pep traces pepTracesList_filtered_minN

by condition

```{r}


complexFeaturesUnique <- getUniqueFeatureGroups(
                            feature_table = scoredDataAll,
                            rt_height = 0,
                            distance_cutoff = 1.25)

complexFeaturesCollapsed <- callapseByUniqueFeatureGroups(
                              feature_table = complexFeaturesUnique,
                              rm_decoys = TRUE)

################' ## Extract feature values
.complex_featureVals_file <- file.path(out_dir, "rdata", "complex_featureVals.RData")
if(!file.exists(.complex_featureVals_file)){

# THIS IS THE STEP THAT STALLS THE COMPLEX SECTION (unnamed-chunk-31, ~76-77%). extractFeatureVals is
# single-threaded and its cost scales with the TRACES it is handed, not with the number of features -
# ~88 min per call on this data whatever the feature count. Handing it the whole peptide trace list
# therefore pays that cost in full, and nothing was written until it finished, so an interrupted run
# lost everything. Ported from the protein-level fix already in this file (and from Ecoli_PCM):
# restrict the traces to the proteins that actually appear in the complex features (a hypothesis set
# covers far fewer proteins than the whole proteome), and checkpoint in chunks so it survives an interrupt.
.brk("complex extractFeatureVals -- SERIAL CCprofiler step, the usual stall point (chunk 31) ...")
.cfv_chunk_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "rdata", "complex_featureVals_chunks")
dir.create(.cfv_chunk_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!exists("complex_featureval_chunks")) complex_featureval_chunks <- 10L

.extract_complex_chunked <- function() {
  FT <- complexFeaturesCollapsed
  idcol <- intersect(c("complex_id", "feature_id", "protein_id"), names(FT))[1]
  if (is.na(idcol)) stop("no id column to split on")
  ids <- unique(as.character(FT[[idcol]]))
  if (length(ids) < 2 * complex_featureval_chunks) stop("too few features to be worth chunking")
  .mk <- file.path(.cfv_chunk_dir, "chunk_count.txt")
  if (file.exists(.mk)) {
    prev <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(readLines(.mk, warn = FALSE)[1]))
    if (is.finite(prev) && prev != complex_featureval_chunks) {
      message("complex_featureval_chunks changed - discarding chunks from the old split.")
      unlink(list.files(.cfv_chunk_dir, pattern = "^chunk_.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE))
    }
  }
  writeLines(as.character(complex_featureval_chunks), .mk)
  grp <- split(ids, cut(seq_along(ids), breaks = complex_featureval_chunks, labels = FALSE))
  # the proteins a chunk needs: subunit accessions of the complexes in that chunk
  pcol <- intersect(c("protein_id", "subunits_detected", "subunits_annotated"), names(FT))[1]
  # SAFETY: if we cannot get subunit proteins, subsetting the traces is impossible and each chunk would
  # silently fall back to the FULL trace list - i.e. pay the full multi-hour cost N times, far worse than
  # one plain call. Bail out (the outer tryCatch then runs a single plain call) rather than risk that.
  if (is.na(pcol)) stop("no subunit column (protein_id/subunits_detected/subunits_annotated) to subset traces by")
  .allprot   <- unique(unlist(strsplit(as.character(FT[[pcol]]), "[;,]\\s*")))
  .traceprot <- tryCatch(unique(pepTracesList_filtered_minN[[1]]$trace_annotation$protein_id), error = function(e) NULL)
  # if the complex subunits cover most of the trace proteins, subsetting saves little and chunking would
  # be slower than one plain call - so bail (the outer tryCatch runs the single plain call).
  if (!length(.allprot)) stop("could not parse any subunit proteins from ", pcol, " - cannot subset traces")
  if (!is.null(.traceprot) && length(.traceprot) &&
      length(intersect(.allprot, .traceprot)) > 0.6 * length(.traceprot))
    stop("subunit subsetting would keep >60% of the trace list - a plain call is cheaper than chunking")
  out <- vector("list", length(grp)); t0 <- Sys.time(); first_new <- TRUE
  for (k in seq_along(grp)) {
    cf <- file.path(.cfv_chunk_dir, sprintf("chunk_%03d.rds", k))
    if (file.exists(cf)) { out[[k]] <- readRDS(cf); next }
    sub <- FT[as.character(FT[[idcol]]) %in% grp[[k]], ]
    prot <- if (!is.na(pcol))
      unique(unlist(strsplit(as.character(sub[[pcol]]), "[;,]\\s*"))) else NULL
    st <- if (!is.null(prot) && length(prot))
      tryCatch(subset(pepTracesList_filtered_minN, trace_subset_ids = prot,
                      trace_subset_type = "protein_id"),
               error = function(e) pepTracesList_filtered_minN) else pepTracesList_filtered_minN
    out[[k]] <- extractFeatureVals(traces = st, features = sub, design_matrix = design_matrix,
                                   extract = "subunits", imputeZero = T, verbose = F)
    saveRDS(out[[k]], cf)
    .brk(sprintf("  complex extractFeatureVals chunk %d/%d done (%.1f min elapsed)", k, length(grp),
                 as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
    if (first_new) {
      .m <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins")); first_new <- FALSE
      .brk(sprintf("  -> first new chunk %.1f min; %d left => about %.1f h to go",
                   .m, length(grp) - k, .m * (length(grp) - k) / 60))
    }
  }
  out <- out[!vapply(out, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (!length(out)) stop("every chunk came back empty")
  if (length(unique(vapply(out, function(z) paste(names(z), collapse = "|"), character(1)))) != 1L)
    stop("chunks disagree on their columns - not safe to combine")
  res <- data.table::rbindlist(out, use.names = TRUE, fill = FALSE)
  if (inherits(out[[1]], "data.table")) res else as.data.frame(res)
}

complex_featureVals <- tryCatch(.extract_complex_chunked(), error = function(e) {
  message("Chunked complex extraction not used (", conditionMessage(e), "); running one plain call.")
  extractFeatureVals(traces = pepTracesList_filtered_minN,
                     features = complexFeaturesCollapsed,
                     design_matrix = design_matrix,
                     extract = "subunits", imputeZero = T, verbose = F)
})
.brk("complex extractFeatureVals DONE")

save(complex_featureVals, file = .complex_featureVals_file)}

  .brk("complex fillFeatureVals DONE and cached")
}
```

# 7. Cross-correlation differential analysis (alternative / complement)

The statistical test above compares **intensity / assembly state** between
conditions. This section is a complementary, shape-based view: for each protein it
compares the **elution profile shape and position** between the two conditions
using the **cross-correlation function (CCF)**.

For every protein we cross-correlate its mean profile in the reference condition
(`strain31`) against the treatment (`strain83`) over a range of fraction lags and
record:

* `max_ccf` — the highest cross-correlation (how similar the two profiles are in
  shape, scale-independent);
* `best_lag` — the lag (in fractions) at which that maximum occurs, i.e. the
  **peak shift** between conditions (0 = no shift);
* `zero_lag_cor` — the correlation with no shift (similarity "as is").

A non-zero `best_lag` (a peak that moves to a different fraction / apparent MW) or
a low similarity flags proteins whose elution behaviour changes between strains —
e.g. complex (dis)assembly — which an abundance-only test can miss.

## 7a. Parameters

```{r ccf-params}
ccf_lag_max         <- 5                       # max shift (fractions) to scan
ccf_shift_threshold <- 1                       # |best_lag| >= this  -> flagged "shifted"
ccf_min_intensity   <- 0                       # require this summed intensity in BOTH conditions
ccf_ref_condition   <- ref_condition           # strain31 (reference)
ccf_treat_condition <- treatment_conditions[1] # strain83 (treatment)
```

## 7b. Per-condition mean elution profiles

```{r ccf-condition-traces}
# Average replicate protein traces within each condition. CCF is scale-invariant,
# so aggr_fun = "sum" (used elsewhere in this pipeline) and "mean" are equivalent
# for the correlation/shift; "sum" is used here because it is known to work with
# this CCprofiler build.
cond_traces <- integrateTraceIntensities(
  protein_traces_list,
  design_matrix    = design_matrix,
  integrate_within = "Condition",
  aggr_fun         = "sum"
)

# Robust extractor: traces$traces -> numeric matrix (proteins x fractions).
.get_trace_matrix <- function(traces_obj) {
  dt <- traces_obj$traces
  frac_cols <- grep("^[0-9]+$", colnames(dt), value = TRUE)
  frac_cols <- frac_cols[order(as.numeric(frac_cols))]
  if (data.table::is.data.table(dt)) {
    m <- as.matrix(dt[, ..frac_cols])
  } else {
    m <- as.matrix(dt[, frac_cols, drop = FALSE])
  }
  rownames(m) <- dt$id
  m
}

ref_mat    <- .get_trace_matrix(cond_traces[[ccf_ref_condition]])
treat_mat  <- .get_trace_matrix(cond_traces[[ccf_treat_condition]])
common_ids <- intersect(rownames(ref_mat), rownames(treat_mat))
message("Cross-correlation over ", length(common_ids), " proteins present in both conditions.")
```

## 7c. Compute the cross-correlation metrics per protein

```{r ccf-compute}
compute_ccf_metrics <- function(x, y, lag_max = 5) {
  x[is.na(x)] <- 0
  y[is.na(y)] <- 0
  if (stats::sd(x) == 0 || stats::sd(y) == 0) {
    return(c(max_ccf = NA_real_, best_lag = NA_real_, zero_lag_cor = NA_real_))
  }
  cc       <- stats::ccf(x, y, lag.max = lag_max, plot = FALSE)
  acf_vals <- as.numeric(cc$acf)
  lags     <- as.numeric(cc$lag)
  i_max    <- which.max(acf_vals)
  zero_i   <- which(lags == 0)
  c(max_ccf      = acf_vals[i_max],
    best_lag     = lags[i_max],
    zero_lag_cor = if (length(zero_i)) acf_vals[zero_i] else NA_real_)
}

ccf_results <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(common_ids, function(id) {
  m <- compute_ccf_metrics(ref_mat[id, ], treat_mat[id, ], lag_max = ccf_lag_max)
  data.table::data.table(
    protein_id   = id,
    max_ccf      = m[["max_ccf"]],
    best_lag     = m[["best_lag"]],
    zero_lag_cor = m[["zero_lag_cor"]],
    int_ref      = sum(ref_mat[id, ],   na.rm = TRUE),
    int_treat    = sum(treat_mat[id, ], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}))

ccf_results[, shifted := (!is.na(best_lag)) &
              (abs(best_lag) >= ccf_shift_threshold) &
              (int_ref   >= ccf_min_intensity) &
              (int_treat >= ccf_min_intensity)]
ccf_results[, log2_int_ratio := log2((int_treat + 1) / (int_ref + 1))]
data.table::setorder(ccf_results, -shifted, -best_lag)

message("Proteins flagged as shifted (|lag| >= ", ccf_shift_threshold, "): ",
        sum(ccf_results$shifted, na.rm = TRUE))
DT::datatable(ccf_results[order(-abs(best_lag))][1:min(.N, 100)],
              caption = "Per-protein cross-correlation metrics (top by |shift|)")
```

## 7d. Diagnostic plots

```{r ccf-plots, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
# Distribution of optimal lags (peak shifts)
print(
  ggplot(ccf_results[!is.na(best_lag)], aes(x = best_lag)) +
    geom_bar(fill = "#4C72B0") + theme_classic() +
    labs(title = "Optimal cross-correlation lag (peak shift) per protein",
         x = "Optimal lag (fractions)   [0 = no shift]", y = "proteins")
)

# Profile-shape similarity (max CCF)
print(
  ggplot(ccf_results[!is.na(max_ccf)], aes(x = max_ccf)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "#55A868") + theme_classic() +
    labs(title = "Maximum cross-correlation (profile-shape similarity)",
         x = "max CCF", y = "proteins")
)

# Shift vs zero-lag similarity, hits highlighted
print(
  ggplot(ccf_results[!is.na(best_lag)],
         aes(x = best_lag, y = zero_lag_cor, color = shifted)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "firebrick")) +
    theme_classic() +
    labs(title = "Elution shift vs zero-lag similarity",
         x = "Optimal lag (fractions)", y = "zero-lag correlation", color = "shifted")
)
```

## 7e. Inspect top shifted proteins (overlaid profiles)

```{r ccf-profile-plots, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
plot_ccf_protein <- function(id) {
  df <- rbind(
    data.frame(fraction = seq_len(ncol(ref_mat)),   intensity = ref_mat[id, ],
               condition = ccf_ref_condition),
    data.frame(fraction = seq_len(ncol(treat_mat)), intensity = treat_mat[id, ],
               condition = ccf_treat_condition)
  )
  mrow <- ccf_results[protein_id == id]
  ggplot(df, aes(x = fraction, y = intensity, color = condition)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1) + theme_classic() +
    labs(title = paste0(id, "   (lag = ", mrow$best_lag,
                        ", maxCCF = ", round(mrow$max_ccf, 2), ")"),
         x = "Fraction", y = "Mean intensity")
}

top_shifted <- head(ccf_results[shifted == TRUE][order(-abs(best_lag))]$protein_id, 12)
for (id in top_shifted) print(plot_ccf_protein(id))
```

## 7f. Complement to the statistical test

```{r ccf-save-and-compare}
# Save the cross-correlation table
write.table(
  ccf_results,
  file      = file.path(out_dir, "tables", "crosscorrelation_results.txt"),
  sep       = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE
)

# If the statistical protein-level differential results exist, cross-tabulate
# which proteins each approach flags (the "complement" view). Adjust the p-value /
# log2FC column names to match your stats table if they differ.
if (exists("protein_DiffExprProtein_list")) {
  stat_dt <- data.table::rbindlist(protein_DiffExprProtein_list, fill = TRUE)
  pcol <- intersect(c("pBHadj", "qVal", "pVal", "global_pBHadj"), names(stat_dt))[1]
  if (!is.na(pcol) && "protein_id" %in% names(stat_dt)) {
    stat_best <- stat_dt[, .(stat_p = min(get(pcol), na.rm = TRUE)), by = protein_id]
    merged    <- merge(ccf_results, stat_best, by = "protein_id", all = TRUE)
    merged[, stat_sig := !is.na(stat_p) & stat_p < 0.05]
    print(table(shifted = merged$shifted, stat_significant = merged$stat_sig, useNA = "ifany"))
    message("Saved comparison-ready table; 'shifted' (cross-correlation) vs ",
            "'stat_significant' (", pcol, " < 0.05) shown above.")
  } else {
    message("Found protein_DiffExprProtein_list but no recognised p-value/protein_id ",
            "column - join ccf_results to it manually on protein_id.")
  }
} else {
  message("Statistical protein-level results not in memory; run section 6's ",
          "differential test, then re-run this chunk to compare the two approaches.")
}
```
